chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Safwan, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who needed wudu for salat but could not find water; he found enough water for his wudu for one hundred or one thousand dirhams, and he had the money. Should he buy it and perform wudu, or perform tayammum? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he should buy. The like of this happened to me, so I bought and performed wudu; and the amount of money spent on that is not large.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying water for wudu if it is scarce?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the hierarchy between using water and performing tayammum when water is scarce but purchasable, establishing that if the cost is not burdensome, one must buy it rather than resorting to dry ablution. Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) validates this ruling by citing his own personal experience, emphasizing that the expense is relatively minor and thus does not constitute a hardship. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation to seek out water persists as long as the financial burden remains manageable, distinguishing it from cases where water is entirely unavailable or prohibitively expensive.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad, from Safwan who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man who is needy to the Ablution (Wudhu) for the Salaat, and he is not able upon the water. So he finds it of a measurement of what he can perform Ablution (Wudhu) with for one hundred Dirhams or for a thousand Dirhams, and he can find (the money) for it. Should he buy and perform Ablution (Wudhu) or perform Tayammum?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should buy. Iasws had come across the like of that, so Iasws bought and performed Ablution (Wudhu); and whatever he buys with that wealth, is a lot’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d from Safwan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who needs to take Wudu’ for Salah (prayer). However, he is not able to find water. He finds a certain amount of water which is enough for his Wudu’ but it costs one hundred dirham or one thousand dirham. He has that much dirham to buy and take Wudu’, should he buy the water or instead take Tayammum? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he must buy. This kind of thing has happened to me and I bought water to take Wudu’. What is bought (in this case) is a great deal.’” (For such Ahadith about an act or issue of the five categories of deeds the qualities such as Wujub, (Obligatory), Hurmat (Prohibited), Istihbab (Preference), Kirahat (Detestability) or Ibahah (Permissibility) one must consult fatwas of one’s Mujtahid.)
